questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस पौधे में नर तथा मादा पुष्प दोनों एक ही पौधे पर पुष्पित होते हैं तथा उनमें सजातपुष्पी परागण अथवा परनिषेचन संभव है ?
questions.text_english: In which of the following plants are both male and female flowers born on the same plant and the mode of pollination can be geitonogamy or xenogamy ?
questions.solution: Maize (Makkа / Zea mays) is a monoecious plant where both male flowers (tassels at the top) and female flowers (silks on the cob) are present on the same plant. This arrangement allows both geitonogamy (pollen from one flower to another flower on the same plant) and xenogamy (cross-pollination from another plant). Papaya and Date Palm are dioecious — male and female flowers are on separate plants — so cross-pollination is the only option. Spinach is also dioecious. Therefore, Maize (C) is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: मक्का (Zea mays) एकलिंगाश्रयी (monoecious) पौधा है जिसमें नर पुष्प (टैसेल) और मादा पुष्प (सिल्क) एक ही पौधे पर होते हैं। इसलिए सजातपुष्पी परागण और परनिषेचन दोनों संभव हैं। पपीता और खजूर द्विलिंगाश्रयी होते हैं, इसलिए विकल्प (C) सही है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा हॉर्मोन मानव अपरा (प्लैसेंटा) द्वारा स्रावित होता है जो सगर्भता (गर्भावस्था) को बनाए रखने में सहायक है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following hormones is secreted by the human placenta that helps in the maintenance of pregnancy ?
questions.solution: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) is secreted by the trophoblast cells of the placenta during early pregnancy. It maintains the corpus luteum, which in turn continues to secrete progesterone, thereby sustaining the uterine lining and maintaining pregnancy. Relaxin is produced by the corpus luteum and helps in parturition. Oxytocin is released from the posterior pituitary and stimulates uterine contractions during labour. Human Placental Lactogen prepares mammary glands for milk production. Hence, hCG (B) is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: मानव जरायु गोनैडोट्रॉपिन (hCG) प्लैसेंटा द्वारा स्रावित होता है जो कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम को बनाए रखता है, जिससे प्रोजेस्टेरोन का स्राव जारी रहता है और गर्भावस्था बनी रहती है। अतः सही उत्तर (B) है।

questions.text: परिवार नियोजन हेतु किसी दंपति द्वारा अपनाई जाने वाली आवधिक संयम अवधि होनी चाहिए :
questions.text_english: The periodic abstinence by a couple for family planning should be from :

options.A: माहवारी चक्र के 5वें से 10वें दिन के बीच
options.B: माहवारी चक्र के 13वें से 15वें दिन के बीच
options.C: माहवारी चक्र के 10वें से 17वें दिन के बीच
options.D: माहवारी चक्र के 16वें से 20वें दिन के बीच

questions.solution: In a 28-day menstrual cycle, ovulation typically occurs around day 14. The safe fertile window is considered from day 10 to day 17, since sperms can survive for 2–3 days inside the female reproductive tract and the egg remains viable for about 1–2 days after ovulation. Couples practising periodic abstinence (rhythm method) must avoid intercourse during this fertile period (day 10 to 17) to prevent pregnancy. Option (C) is therefore correct.
questions.solution_hindi: 28 दिन के मासिक चक्र में ओव्यूलेशन लगभग 14वें दिन होता है। दिन 10 से 17 तक का काल उर्वर काल (fertile period) होता है, अतः दंपति को इन दिनों में संभोग से बचना चाहिए। इसलिए सही उत्तर (C) है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित से गलत जोड़े का चयन कीजिए :
मानव कैरियोटाइप — लक्षण
(A) 45 + XX — चौड़ी हथेली में अभिलाक्षणिक पाम क्रीज़
(B) 44 + XXY — समग्र रूप से मादा लक्षण का विकास
(C) 44 + XO — अल्पवर्धित अंडाशय के कारण नारी बाँझ होती है
(D) 44 + XY — सामान्य नर (पुरुष)
questions.text_english:
Select the incorrect match from the following :
Human Karyotype — Characters
(A) 45 + XX — Broad palm with characteristic palm crease
(B) 44 + XXY — Overall feminine development
(C) 44 + XO — Sterile females as ovaries are rudimentary
(D) 44 + XY — Normal male

options.A: 45 + XX — चौड़ी हथेली में अभिलाक्षणिक पाम क्रीज़
options.B: 44 + XXY — समग्र रूप से मादा लक्षण का विकास
options.C: 44 + XO — अल्पवर्धित अंडाशय के कारण नारी बाँझ होती है

options_english.A: 45 + XX — Broad palm with characteristic palm crease
options_english.C: 44 + XO — Sterile females as ovaries are rudimentary

questions.solution: 44 + XXY corresponds to Klinefelter's syndrome, which affects males. These individuals have an overall masculine body but show some feminine features such as gynaecomastia (development of breast tissue); they do NOT show overall feminine development. Overall feminine development is a characteristic of Turner's syndrome (44 + XO) females, not Klinefelter's. 45 + XX (47,XX with extra chromosome, i.e., Down syndrome female) showing broad palm with characteristic crease is correct. 44 + XO (Turner's) showing sterile females is correct. 44 + XY is the normal male karyotype. Hence, the incorrect match is (B).
questions.solution_hindi: 44 + XXY क्लाइनफेल्टर सिंड्रोम है जो पुरुषों में होता है। इसमें समग्र रूप से मादा लक्षण नहीं, बल्कि पुरुषों में कुछ स्त्री-लक्षण (जैसे गाइनेकोमेस्टिया) पाए जाते हैं। अतः गलत जोड़ा (B) है।

questions.text: आप जानते ही हैं कि प्राकृतिक रूप से बीस भिन्न प्रकार के ऐमीनो अम्ल पाए जाते हैं तथा डीएनए में चार भिन्न प्रकार के क्षार पाए जाते हैं। ऐसे 3 क्षारों का समूह एक विशिष्ट ऐमीनो अम्ल का कूट लेखन करता है। यदि ऐसा न होकर 96 भिन्न प्रकार के ऐमीनो अम्ल होते तथा डीएनए में 12 भिन्न प्रकार के क्षार होते, तो एक प्रकूट के संयोजन हेतु आवश्यक न्यूनतम क्षारों की संख्या होगी :
questions.text_english: You know that there are twenty different types of naturally occurring amino acids and four different types of bases in the DNA. A combination of 3 such bases code for a specific amino acid. If instead there are 96 different amino acids and 12 different bases in the DNA, then the minimum number of combination of bases required to form a codon is :
questions.solution: We need the minimum codon length (n) such that 12^n ≥ 96. If n = 1: 12^1 = 12, which is less than 96. If n = 2: 12^2 = 144, which is greater than 96. So the minimum number of bases required to form a codon is 2. This is analogous to the natural scenario where 4^3 = 64 ≥ 20, giving a triplet code. Here, 12^2 = 144 ≥ 96, so a doublet (2-base codon) is sufficient. Hence, the correct answer is (C) 2.
questions.solution_hindi: 12^2 = 144 ≥ 96 होता है, अतः 12 प्रकार के क्षारों के साथ 96 ऐमीनो अम्लों को कोड करने के लिए न्यूनतम 2 क्षारों की आवश्यकता होगी। सही उत्तर (C) है।

questions.text: एक योजनात्मक पॉलीन्यूक्लियोटाइड शृंखला में '– – – –' लाइन इसके प्रकार बंध का निरूपण दर्शाती है :
questions.text_english: The type of bond represented by the dotted line '– – – –' in a schematic polynucleotide chain is :
questions.solution: In a polynucleotide chain, consecutive nucleotides are linked together through phosphodiester bonds, where the phosphate group forms ester bonds with the 3' carbon of one sugar and the 5' carbon of the next sugar. In the schematic diagram, the dotted lines between P (phosphate) and S (sugar) units represent these phosphodiester bonds. Hydrogen bonds occur between the two complementary strands of DNA (between bases). N-glycosidic bonds link the nitrogenous base to the sugar. Peptide bonds are found in proteins, not DNA. Hence, the answer is (D) Phosphodiester bond.
questions.solution_hindi: पॉलीन्यूक्लियोटाइड शृंखला में फॉस्फेट समूह, एक शर्करा के 3' कार्बन और अगली शर्करा के 5' कार्बन से एस्टर बंध बनाता है — इसे ही फॉस्फोडाइएस्टर बंध कहते हैं। आरेख में डैश (-–) रेखाएं इसी बंध को दर्शाती हैं। अतः उत्तर (D) है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस प्रकार की परिस्थितियों/रोग में मानव शरीर में मास्ट कोशिकाओं की अतिक्रियाशीलता (में वृद्धि) प्रेक्षित होती है ?
questions.text_english: In which of the following conditions/diseases is there a substantial increase in the activity of mast cells observed in the human body ?
questions.solution: Mast cells are tissue-resident immune cells that play a central role in allergic reactions. During an allergic response, IgE antibodies produced against an allergen bind to receptors on mast cells. When the allergen is encountered again, it cross-links the IgE antibodies on mast cells, triggering them to degranulate and release chemicals such as histamine. This causes the symptoms of allergy (sneezing, watery eyes, redness, etc.). Typhoid is caused by Salmonella typhi (bacterial infection), Ascariasis is caused by Ascaris lumbricoides (helminth infection), and AIDS suppresses immune cells. None of these specifically overactivate mast cells. Hence, the correct answer is (B) Allergy.
questions.solution_hindi: एलर्जी में IgE एंटीबॉडी, मास्ट कोशिकाओं पर बँध जाती हैं। पुनः एलर्जन के संपर्क में आने पर मास्ट कोशिकाएं हिस्टामिन आदि रसायन छोड़ती हैं। अतः सही उत्तर (B) एलर्जी है।

questions.text: दूध को दही में स्कंदित करने वाले लैक्टोबैसिलस को सामान्यतः इस वर्ग में रखते हैं :
questions.text_english: Lactobacillus that sets milk into curd is categorised as :
questions.solution: Lactobacillus is a heterotrophic bacterium because it obtains its energy and carbon from organic compounds (i.e., lactose in milk) and cannot synthesise its own food. It ferments lactose into lactic acid, which causes the curdling of milk. Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophs. Archaebacteria live in extreme environments. Chemosynthetic bacteria obtain energy from inorganic chemical reactions. Since Lactobacillus depends on organic matter for nutrition, it is correctly classified as heterotrophic bacteria. The answer is (D).
questions.solution_hindi: लैक्टोबैसिलस एक विषमपोषी जीवाणु है क्योंकि यह कार्बनिक पदार्थ (दूध की शर्करा) से ऊर्जा प्राप्त करता है और दुग्ध शर्करा को लैक्टिक अम्ल में किण्वित करता है। अतः सही उत्तर (D) है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित पारजीवी जंतुओं (ट्रांसजेनिक एनिमल्स) में से किसे पोलियो के टीके (वैक्सीन) की सुरक्षा परीक्षण हेतु उपयोग किया गया है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following transgenic animals is being used to test the safety of the polio vaccine ?
questions.solution: Transgenic mice have been developed that are susceptible to poliovirus infection and are used to test the safety and efficacy of the polio vaccine. Normal mice are not naturally susceptible to polio, but transgenic mice expressing the human poliovirus receptor (CD155) can be infected, making them ideal models for safety testing. Sheep (Dolly) have been used for cloning studies. Goats and pigs have been used for production of pharmaceutical proteins in milk. Hence, the correct answer is (D) Mice.
questions.solution_hindi: पारजीवी चूहों में मानव पोलियोवायरस रिसेप्टर प्रविष्ट किया गया है जिससे वे पोलियो से संक्रमित हो सकते हैं। इन्हें पोलियो वैक्सीन की सुरक्षा परीक्षण के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है। अतः सही उत्तर (D) चूहा है।

questions.text: प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज़ – हिंड II डीएनए अणु के विशिष्ट अनुक्रम को पहचान कर विशेष बिन्दु पर काटते हैं, इस विशिष्ट अनुक्रम में क्षारक युग्मों की संख्या है :
questions.text_english: Restriction Endonuclease – Hind II always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point by recognising a specific sequence of :
questions.solution: Hind II was the first restriction endonuclease to be discovered. It recognises a specific palindromic sequence of six base pairs — GTY↓RAC (where Y = pyrimidine and R = purine) — and cuts the DNA at that particular site. This was a landmark discovery in molecular biology. Most common restriction enzymes (like EcoRI, HindIII) recognise 4-6 base pair sequences. Hence, the correct answer is (A) Six base pairs.
questions.solution_hindi: हिंड II प्रतिबंधन एंजाइम DNA में 6 क्षारक युग्मों के विशिष्ट अनुक्रम को पहचानकर उसे काटता है। यह पहला खोजा गया प्रतिबंधन एंजाइम था। सही उत्तर (A) छह क्षारक युग्म है।

questions.text: वह समुन्नत विशेषक जो आनुवंशिकत: रूपांतरित पारजीवी फसल – गोल्डन राइस में पाया जाता है :
questions.text_english: The improved trait that is found in the genetically modified transgenic crop Golden rice is :
questions.solution: Golden rice is a transgenic variety of rice that has been engineered to produce beta-carotene (a precursor of Vitamin A) in the endosperm of the grain, which gives it its characteristic golden colour. It was developed to address Vitamin A deficiency, which causes blindness and immune deficiency in millions of children worldwide. High lysine content is a trait in some transgenic maize varieties. Bt cotton and Bt brinjal are insect-resistant crops. Hence, the correct answer is (D) High vitamin-A content.
questions.solution_hindi: गोल्डन राइस एक पारजीवी चावल है जिसे बीटा-कैरोटीन (विटामिन-A का अग्रदूत) उत्पन्न करने के लिए आनुवंशिक रूप से रूपांतरित किया गया है। इसलिए सही उत्तर (D) विटामिन-ए की उच्च मात्रा है।

questions.text: उपभोक्ताओं द्वारा नवीन कार्बनिक पदार्थों के निर्माण, तथा शाकाहारियों एवं अपघटकों के लिए भी उपभोग हेतु उपलब्ध जैव मात्रा को क्रमशः निम्न प्रकार से व्यक्त करते हैं :
questions.text_english: The rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers, and the biomass available for consumption of herbivores as well as decomposers are referred to as :

options.A: सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता तथा नेट प्राथमिक उत्पादकता
options.B: नेट प्राथमिक उत्पादकता तथा द्वितीयक उत्पादकता
options.C: द्वितीयक उत्पादकता तथा नेट प्राथमिक उत्पादकता
options.D: द्वितीयक उत्पादकता तथा सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता

options_english.A: Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity
options_english.B: Net primary productivity and Secondary productivity
options_english.C: Secondary productivity and Net primary productivity
options_english.D: Secondary productivity and Gross primary productivity

questions.solution: Secondary productivity refers to the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers (heterotrophs). Net primary productivity (NPP) is the biomass that remains after the autotrophs have used some for their own respiration — it is this NPP that is available for consumption by herbivores and decomposers. Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the total photosynthetic production. The question asks for the rate of organic matter formed by consumers (= Secondary productivity) and the biomass available for herbivores and decomposers (= Net primary productivity). Hence, the correct answer is (C).
questions.solution_hindi: उपभोक्ताओं द्वारा नवीन कार्बनिक पदार्थ निर्माण की दर को द्वितीयक उत्पादकता कहते हैं। शाकाहारियों तथा अपघटकों के लिए उपलब्ध जैव मात्रा नेट प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) है। अतः सही उत्तर (C) है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : हमारे देश का कानून शिशु को कानूनन गोद लेने की इजाज़त देता है और यह आज भी संतानविहीन दंपति के लिए जनकता प्राप्ति का सर्वोत्तम उपाय है।
कारण (R) : भारत में अनाथ और दीन-हीन बच्चों को कानूनी रूप से गोद लेने में भावनात्मक, धार्मिक तथा सामाजिक घटक बाधक नहीं हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): The laws of our country permit legal adoption and it is as yet, one of the best methods for childless couples looking for parenthood.
Reason (R): Emotional, religious and social factors are no deterrents to the legal adoption of orphaned and destitute children in India.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों में से सही उत्तर चुनें
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D)

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The Assertion (A) is true — Indian law does permit legal adoption and it remains one of the best methods for childless couples to become parents. However, the Reason (R) is false — in practice, emotional, religious, and social factors do act as significant deterrents to the legal adoption of orphaned and destitute children in India. Many families prefer biological children and social stigmas persist. Since A is true but R is false, the correct answer is (C).
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है क्योंकि भारत में कानूनन गोद लेना वैध है। परन्तु कारण (R) असत्य है क्योंकि वास्तव में भावनात्मक, धार्मिक और सामाजिक कारण गोद लेने में बाधा डालते हैं। अतः सही उत्तर (C) है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : संलग्न जीन F2 में द्विसंकर अनुपात 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 नहीं दर्शाते (परिलक्षित नहीं होते) हैं।
कारण (R) : संलग्न (सहलग्न) जीनों में स्वतंत्र विसंयोजन नहीं होता।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Linked genes do not show dihybrid F2 ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
Reason (R): Linked genes do not undergo independent assortment.

questions.solution: The naturalist is Jean Baptiste de Lamarck. The picture of giraffes illustrates Lamarck's Theory of Inheritance of Acquired Characters. questions.solution: In the ART (IVF-ET) programme, eggs are first collected from the female partner after ovarian stimulation using hormones. Sperms are separately collected from the male partner. questions.text_english: Explain the mode of action of contraceptive pills taken by human females. Mention the schedule to be followed for effective outcome.

key_points: Contain synthetic progesterone and/or oestrogen
Inhibit ovulation by suppressing LH and FSH secretion from the pituitary
Alter uterine endometrium to prevent implantation
Schedule: one pill daily for 21 days starting from the 5th day of the menstrual cycle, followed by a 7-day gap, then repeated

questions.solution: Oral contraceptive pills contain synthetic hormones — either a combination of oestrogen and progesterone, or progesterone alone. These hormones act by inhibiting the secretion of FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) and LH (Luteinising Hormone) from the anterior pituitary gland. Without adequate FSH, follicle development is suppressed and without the LH surge, ovulation does not occur. Additionally, the altered hormonal environment changes the uterine endometrium, making it unfavourable for implantation. The schedule to be followed is: one pill is taken daily for 21 days starting from the 5th day of the menstrual cycle. After 21 days, there is a gap of 7 days (during which withdrawal bleeding occurs), and then the next course begins. Consistent adherence to this schedule is essential for effectiveness.

sub_questions.text_english: Name and write two characteristics of the type of DNA that forms the basis of DNA fingerprinting technique.

key_points: Satellite DNA / Repetitive DNA / VNTRs (Variable Number Tandem Repeats)
Characteristic 1: Highly repetitive short sequences present in non-coding regions of DNA
Characteristic 2: Show high degree of polymorphism — the number of repeats varies from individual to individual

sub_questions.solution: The DNA used as the basis of DNA fingerprinting is called Satellite DNA or Repetitive DNA, specifically VNTRs (Variable Number of Tandem Repeats). Its two characteristics are: (1) It consists of short nucleotide sequences repeated many times in tandem, present mainly in non-coding regions of the genome. (2) It shows high degree of polymorphism — the number of repeat units at each VNTR locus varies greatly between individuals, making each person's DNA pattern unique (except identical twins).

sub_questions.text: इस तकनीक के कोई दो अनुप्रयोगों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two applications of this technique.

key_points: Forensic science: identifying criminals from biological evidence left at crime scenes
Determining paternity/maternity in disputed parentage cases

sub_questions.solution: Two applications of DNA fingerprinting are: (1) Forensic science — DNA fingerprinting is used to identify suspects in criminal cases by matching DNA from hair, blood, or other biological samples found at crime scenes with the suspect's DNA. (2) Paternity testing — it is used to determine whether a given man is the biological father of a child by comparing DNA patterns of the child, mother, and alleged father.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the significance of the experiment carried out by S.L. Miller. Name the scientists whose hypothesis prompted him to carry out this experiment.

key_points: Miller simulated early Earth conditions (electric sparks as energy source, reducing atmosphere of CH4, NH3, H2, H2O vapour)
He observed formation of amino acids and other organic molecules
This showed that abiotic synthesis of organic molecules is possible
Scientists: Oparin and Haldane (proposed the chemical evolution hypothesis)

sub_questions.solution: S.L. Miller's experiment (1953) was significant because it demonstrated for the first time that organic molecules — including amino acids — could be synthesised abiotically under conditions simulating the early Earth's atmosphere. He created a closed system with water, methane, ammonia, and hydrogen and subjected the mixture to electric sparks (simulating lightning). After a week, he detected several amino acids such as glycine and alanine. This supported the hypothesis of chemical origin of life. The scientists whose hypothesis prompted him were A.I. Oparin and J.B.S. Haldane, who had proposed that the primitive atmosphere was reducing and that organic molecules could have formed spontaneously.

sub_questions.solution: Analysis of meteorites, such as the Murchison meteorite, has revealed the presence of amino acids and other complex organic molecules. This shows that abiotic synthesis of organic molecules is not restricted to Earth alone and can occur in outer space under appropriate chemical conditions. This strongly supports the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis that the building blocks of life could have been formed abiotically.

questions.text_english: In a family, the father, the daughter and the son are colour blind, whereas the mother has normal vision. Do you think the son and the daughter have inherited the disease from their father ? Work out a cross to justify your answer.

key_points: Colour blindness is X-linked recessive
Father: X^c Y (colour blind); Mother: X^C X^c (carrier, normal vision)
Son gets Y from father and X from mother; son is colour blind means he got X^c from mother, NOT from father
Daughter gets X from father (X^c) AND X from mother; daughter is colour blind means both X chromosomes carry recessive allele
Conclusion: Son inherited colour blindness from mother (carrier). Daughter inherited one X^c from father and one X^c from mother

questions.solution:
Colour blindness is an X-linked recessive disorder. Father is colour blind: X^cY. Mother has normal vision but since her son is colour blind, she must be a carrier: X^C X^c.

Cross: X^cY (father) × X^C X^c (mother)
Offspring: X^C X^c (normal carrier daughter), X^c X^c (colour blind daughter), X^C Y (normal son), X^c Y (colour blind son)

For the SON: Sons receive their Y chromosome from the father and their X chromosome from the mother. The son's colour blindness (X^cY) came from the mother's X^c, NOT from the father. So the son did NOT inherit colour blindness from the father.

For the DAUGHTER: Daughters receive one X from each parent. The colour-blind daughter (X^cX^c) received one X^c from the father and one X^c from the carrier mother. So the daughter inherited colour blindness partially from both parents — the recessive allele came from both father AND mother.
questions.solution_hindi: वर्णांधता X-सहलग्न अप्रभावी विकार है। पिता: X^cY; माँ (वाहक): X^C X^c। पुत्र को Y पिता से और X माँ से मिलती है — पुत्र की वर्णांधता माँ से आई है। पुत्री को एक X पिता से (X^c) और एक X माँ से (X^c) मिली — पुत्री की वर्णांधता दोनों से आई है। अतः पुत्र की वर्णांधता पिता से नहीं, माँ से आई है, और पुत्री की दोनों से।

sub_questions.solution: The first transgenic cow was named Rosie. This has significant importance in providing better infant nutrition.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the convention for naming EcoRI.

key_points: E = Escherichia (genus of bacterium)
co = coli (species name)
R = RY13 (strain of the bacterium)
I = first enzyme isolated from this strain (Roman numeral)

sub_questions.solution: EcoRI is named based on the following convention: E stands for the genus Escherichia; co stands for the species coli; R stands for the strain RY13 from which the enzyme was isolated; and I (Roman numeral one) indicates that it was the first restriction enzyme isolated from that particular strain. This naming system ensures each restriction enzyme is uniquely identified by its source organism and isolation order.

sub_questions.text_english: With the help of an illustration only, show the action of EcoRI on a DNA Polynucleotide.

key_points: EcoRI recognises palindromic sequence 5'-GAATTC-3' / 3'-CTTAAG-5'
Cuts between G and A on both strands to produce sticky ends (overhangs): 5'-G and AATTC-3'

sub_questions.solution:
EcoRI recognises the palindromic sequence 5'-GAATTC-3' on both strands. It cuts the DNA between G and A on each strand:
5'...G | AATTC...3'
3'...CTTAA | G...5'
This produces two DNA fragments each with a 5' overhang of AATT (sticky ends), which can later be joined with complementary sticky ends by DNA ligase.

(b) Describe co-evolution with the help of this example.

sub_questions.text: यह कैसे सुनिश्चित होता है कि आर्किड ऑफ्रीस का परागण एक विशिष्ट जाति की मक्खिका द्वारा ही हो ?
sub_questions.text_english: Explain how it is ensured that the orchid Ophrys is pollinated by a specific species of bee.

key_points: One petal of Ophrys mimics the female bee in shape, colour, pattern, and texture
The flower also produces chemicals that mimic the sex pheromones of the female bee
The male bee, mistaking the flower for a female, attempts to mate with it (pseudocopulation)
In doing so, pollen gets attached to the bee and is transferred to another Ophrys flower, ensuring pollination only by that specific bee species

sub_questions.solution: The orchid Ophrys ensures pollination by a specific bee species through a remarkable mimicry strategy. One of its petals has evolved to closely resemble the female of a specific bee species in shape, colour, and surface texture. Additionally, the flower secretes chemical compounds that mimic the sex pheromones (chemical signals) of the female bee. Attracted by both visual and chemical cues, the male bee lands on the flower and attempts to mate with it — a process called pseudocopulation. During this attempt, pollen masses (pollinia) attach to the bee's body. When the bee visits another Ophrys flower and repeats the pseudocopulation attempt, the pollen is transferred, achieving cross-pollination. Only the specific bee species is attracted by this particular combination of mimicry and pheromones, ensuring species-specific pollination.

sub_questions.text: इस उदाहरण की सहायता से सह-विकास का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe co-evolution with the help of this example.

key_points: Co-evolution is the process where two species exert selection pressure on each other and evolve together
Ophrys and its specific bee have co-evolved — any change in the bee's appearance or pheromone profile is matched by a corresponding change in the orchid's mimicry

sub_questions.solution: Co-evolution refers to the process where two different species reciprocally influence each other's evolution through mutual selection pressures. In the Ophrys-bee example, the orchid has evolved its petal shape and chemical pheromones to precisely mimic the female of a specific bee species. Any evolutionary change in the bee's pheromone profile or morphology creates a selection pressure on the orchid to also evolve correspondingly. This mutual evolutionary adaptation of both species to each other over generations is co-evolution.

sub_questions.solution: Region III has maximum species richness because it likely represents a tropical region. sub_questions.text_english: Plants and animals do not have uniform diversity in the world but show rather uneven distribution. Mention what this kind of diversity is referred to as.

key_points: Alpha diversity / Beta diversity / Gamma diversity — the uneven distribution of species across different regions is referred to as Beta diversity

sub_questions.solution: The uneven distribution of species diversity across different geographic regions and habitats is referred to as Beta diversity (between-habitat diversity). It measures the change in species composition between different habitats or regions. High beta diversity indicates that species are distributed unevenly across the landscape.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is it that prokaryotes do not have an estimated number of their species diversity as seen in plants and animals ? Explain.

key_points: Prokaryotes do not follow the biological species concept strictly
They reproduce asexually and undergo horizontal gene transfer, making species boundaries difficult to define
Most prokaryotes cannot be cultured in the laboratory, so they cannot be studied or counted the way plants and animals are

sub_questions.solution: Prokaryotes do not have an estimated number of species like plants and animals for two main reasons. First, prokaryotes reproduce primarily by binary fission (asexual reproduction) and frequently exchange genes through horizontal gene transfer, making it very difficult to define species boundaries using the conventional biological species concept. Second, the vast majority of prokaryotes — estimated at over 99% — cannot be cultured in laboratory conditions. Since most studies of biodiversity rely on culturing and morphological identification, prokaryotic diversity remains largely unexplored and uncountable, unlike plants and animals which can be observed, collected, and classified.

sub_questions.text_english: What are the sites in a plasmid called where ampicillin and tetracycline resistance genes are inserted ? State their role in genetic engineering.

key_points: These sites are called Selectable Marker genes

Role: They help in selecting transformed (recombinant) bacteria from non-transformed ones; bacteria that have taken up the plasmid will show resistance to the antibiotic corresponding to the intact marker gene

sub_questions.solution: The sites in a plasmid where antibiotic resistance genes (such as those for ampicillin and tetracycline) are inserted are called Selectable Markers. In genetic engineering, selectable markers play a crucial role in identifying and selecting transformed bacteria. When the foreign gene is inserted into one of these markers (e.g., tetracycline resistance gene), it is disrupted. Bacteria that have taken up the recombinant plasmid will be ampicillin-resistant but tetracycline-sensitive, while non-transformed bacteria will be sensitive to ampicillin. This allows researchers to identify and select recombinant colonies efficiently.

sub_questions.text_english: Name two enzymes playing an important role in genetic engineering. [OR: State the role of β-galactosidase in insertional inactivation.]

key_points: Restriction endonuclease and DNA ligase

OR: β-galactosidase converts colourless substrate X-gal into a blue product; when the foreign gene is inserted into the lacZ gene, β-galactosidase production is disrupted and recombinant colonies appear white, while non-recombinant colonies appear blue

sub_questions.solution:
Two enzymes playing important roles in genetic engineering are (1) Restriction Endonuclease, which cuts DNA at specific palindromic sequences to produce fragments with defined ends, and (2) DNA Ligase, which joins the cut DNA fragments together to form a recombinant DNA molecule.

Alternately (OR): β-galactosidase is encoded by the lacZ gene. In insertional inactivation, if a foreign DNA fragment is inserted into the lacZ gene, the enzyme's activity is lost. When X-gal (a chromogenic substrate) is added to the agar, normal (non-recombinant) colonies produce active β-galactosidase which turns X-gal blue, while recombinant colonies cannot produce the enzyme and therefore remain white. This blue-white screening allows easy identification of recombinant clones.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the development of male gametophyte in an angiosperm.

key_points: Microsporogenesis: microspore mother cells undergo meiosis to form 4 haploid microspores (tetrad)
Each microspore develops a two-layered wall: exine (outer) and intine (inner)
The microspore nucleus divides mitotically to form a large vegetative cell (tube cell) and a small generative cell — this is the 2-celled pollen grain
Before or after shedding, the generative cell divides to form two male gametes — this is the 3-celled pollen grain
On landing on stigma, the pollen germinates, tube cell grows a pollen tube, and the two male gametes travel down

sub_questions.solution: In angiosperms, the development of male gametophyte begins in the anther. The microsporocytes (microspore mother cells) present in the microsporangium undergo meiosis to produce four haploid microspores arranged in a tetrad. Each microspore develops a thick outer wall (exine made of sporopollenin) and a thin inner wall (intine of cellulose and pectin). The haploid microspore nucleus then undergoes mitosis to produce a large vegetative (tube) cell and a small generative cell — this constitutes the two-celled or immature pollen grain. Before or after the pollen is shed, the generative cell undergoes another mitotic division to produce two haploid male gametes. This three-celled pollen grain is the mature male gametophyte. When pollen lands on a compatible stigma, the vegetative cell germinates and grows a pollen tube through the style; the two male gametes travel down the pollen tube to the ovule for double fertilisation.

sub_questions.text_english: At which stage of life are primary follicles formed in a human female ?

key_points: Primary follicles are formed during foetal development (before birth), in the ovary of the foetus itself

sub_questions.solution: Primary follicles in a human female are formed during foetal development, i.e., before birth. The ovary of a developing female foetus contains about 2 million primary oocytes (each surrounded by granulosa cells to form primary follicles), which are arrested in prophase I of meiosis. This number decreases progressively throughout life.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the events (both hormonal and structural) that occur at the time of ovulation till the onset of the next menstrual cycle.

key_points: LH surge triggers ovulation (release of secondary oocyte from Graafian follicle) around day 14
Ruptured follicle transforms into corpus luteum under influence of LH
Corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone and some oestrogen
Progesterone maintains endometrium for implantation
If fertilisation does not occur, corpus luteum degenerates into corpus albicans
Fall in progesterone and oestrogen causes endometrium to break down — onset of menstruation (next cycle begins)

sub_questions.solution: At ovulation (approximately day 14), a surge in LH (Luteinising Hormone) causes the mature Graafian follicle to rupture and release the secondary oocyte (ovum). After ovulation, the ruptured follicle undergoes structural transformation under continued LH influence to form the corpus luteum (yellow body). The corpus luteum secretes large quantities of progesterone and also some oestrogen, which maintain and thicken the uterine endometrium in preparation for implantation. If fertilisation and implantation do not occur, the corpus luteum degenerates after about 14 days, transforming into the corpus albicans (white body). The resultant sharp decline in progesterone and oestrogen levels causes the endometrial lining to break down and shed, marking the onset of menstruation and the beginning of the next menstrual cycle.

sub_questions.text_english: Stability, as one of the properties of genetic material, was very evident in one of the very early experiments in genetics. Name the scientist and describe his experiment. State the conclusion he arrived at.

key_points: Scientist: Frederick Griffith (Griffith's transformation experiment, 1928)
Used two strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae: virulent smooth (S) strain and non-virulent rough (R) strain
Injected live S — mice died; live R — mice survived; heat-killed S — mice survived; heat-killed S + live R — mice died
The R bacteria had been transformed into S bacteria by a transforming principle from heat-killed S cells

Conclusion: Some stable chemical substance (the transforming principle) from the S strain passed into R bacteria, transforming them permanently and hereditarily — this showed stability of genetic material

sub_questions.solution:
The scientist is Frederick Griffith, who performed his famous transformation experiment in 1928 using Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteria.

Griffith used two strains: the virulent smooth (S) strain with a polysaccharide capsule, and the non-virulent rough (R) strain without a capsule. When he injected live S-strain bacteria into mice, they developed pneumonia and died. When he injected live R-strain bacteria, the mice survived. When he injected heat-killed S-strain bacteria, the mice also survived. However, when he injected a mixture of heat-killed S-strain and live R-strain bacteria, the mice died — and live S-strain bacteria were recovered from the dead mice.

Griffith concluded that some stable 'transforming principle' had been transferred from the heat-killed S bacteria to the live R bacteria, permanently converting (transforming) them into the virulent S type. This transformation was inherited by subsequent generations of bacteria, demonstrating that the genetic material is stable and can be transferred between organisms. (Later, Avery, MacLeod and McCarty proved the transforming principle was DNA.)

sub_questions.text_english: A tall pea plant bearing violet flowers with unknown genotype is given. Find the genotype by working out different crosses only by selfing the plants. Write the genotypic and phenotypic ratios of each cross shown by you.

key_points: Tall (T_) and violet flower (V_) are both dominant; possible genotypes are TTVV, TTVv, TtVV, TtVv
If selfing gives all tall violet offspring → homozygous dominant for both (TTVV or pure line)
If selfing gives 3 tall violet : 1 dwarf violet → TtVV (heterozygous for height, homozygous for flower colour)
If selfing gives 3 tall violet : 1 tall white → TTVv or TtVv (heterozygous for flower colour)
If selfing gives 9 tall violet : 3 dwarf violet : 3 tall white : 1 dwarf white → TtVv (dihybrid)

sub_questions.solution:
Let T = tall (dominant), t = dwarf (recessive); V = violet (dominant), v = white (recessive).

A tall violet plant can have genotype TTVV, TTVv, TtVV, or TtVv.

To determine the genotype, self the plant and observe F1 offspring:

Case 1: If selfing (TTVV × TTVV) gives all tall violet plants — Genotypic ratio: 1 TTVV; Phenotypic ratio: all tall violet (1:0). Conclusion: plant is TTVV.

Case 2: If selfing (TtVV × TtVV) gives 1 tall violet : 2 tall violet : 1 dwarf violet — Genotypic ratio: 1 TTVV : 2 TtVV : 1 ttvv; Phenotypic ratio: 3 tall violet : 1 dwarf violet. Conclusion: plant is TtVV.

Case 3: If selfing (TTVv × TTVv) gives — Genotypic ratio: 1 TTVV : 2 TTVv : 1 TTvv; Phenotypic ratio: 3 tall violet : 1 tall white. Conclusion: plant is TTVv.

Case 4: If selfing (TtVv × TtVv) gives — Genotypic ratio: 9 T_V_ : 3 T_vv : 3 ttV_ : 1 ttvv; Phenotypic ratio: 9 tall violet : 3 tall white : 3 dwarf violet : 1 dwarf white. Conclusion: plant is TtVv.

sub_questions.text: कोशिकाओं के उस अभिलक्षण का नाम लिखकर व्याख्या कीजिए जो प्रसामान्य कोशिकाओं में तो अभिलक्षित होता है परन्तु कैंसर कोशिकाओं में लुप्त हो जाता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Name and explain the property present in normal cells but is lost in cancer cells.

key_points: Property: Contact inhibition
Normal cells stop dividing when they come into contact with other cells (contact inhibition)
Cancer cells lose contact inhibition and continue to divide uncontrollably, piling up into tumour masses

sub_questions.solution: The property is Contact Inhibition. In normal cells, when a dividing cell comes into contact with its neighbouring cells, the cell-to-cell contact sends signals that inhibit further division — this is contact inhibition. Cancer cells lose this property of contact inhibition. As a result, cancer cells continue to divide uncontrollably even when surrounded by other cells, forming masses of cells called tumours. This unrestricted proliferation is the hallmark of cancer.

sub_questions.text: मानव की सभी प्रसामान्य कोशिकाओं में वे जीन होते हैं जो विशिष्ट परिस्थितियों में कैंसरजनी हो सकते हैं। उनका नाम लिखिए तथा बताइए कि वे कैसे उपर्युक्त रूप में व्यवहार करते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: All normal human cells have genes that may become cancerous under certain conditions. Name them and explain how.

key_points: These genes are called Proto-oncogenes (cellular oncogenes)
Under normal conditions they regulate cell growth and division
When mutated or over-expressed (due to radiation, chemicals, viruses), they become oncogenes and cause uncontrolled cell division leading to cancer

sub_questions.solution: These genes are called Proto-oncogenes (or cellular oncogenes). In normal cells, proto-oncogenes regulate and promote normal cell growth and division in a controlled manner. Under certain conditions — such as exposure to radiation, chemical carcinogens, or viruses — these proto-oncogenes can undergo mutations or become overexpressed. When mutated, they are called oncogenes. Oncogenes produce overactive or continuously active growth-promoting proteins, driving the cell into uncontrolled division and leading to cancer.

sub_questions.text: जीवूतिपरीक्षा (बायोप्सी) तथा ऊतक विकृति (हिस्टोपैथोलॉजी) की कैंसर के अभिज्ञान तथा निदान में भूमिका।
sub_questions.text_english: State the role of Biopsy and Histopathology in detection and diagnosis of cancer.

key_points: A thin slice of suspected tumour tissue is removed (biopsy) and stained
Examined under microscope (histopathology) to detect cancerous cells based on their altered morphology, abnormal nucleus, and disorganised structure

sub_questions.solution: In biopsy, a small piece of tissue is surgically removed from the suspected tumour site. This tissue is then processed, thinly sectioned, stained, and examined under a microscope (histopathology). Cancerous cells show characteristic changes such as enlarged irregular nuclei, loss of cell organisation, and abnormal mitotic figures. This examination allows pathologists to confirm the presence and type of cancer.

sub_questions.text: चुम्बकीय अनुनादी इमेजिंग (मैग्नेटिक रेज़ोनेंस इमेजिंग) की कैंसर के अभिज्ञान तथा निदान में भूमिका।
sub_questions.text_english: State the role of Magnetic Resonance Imaging in detection and diagnosis of cancer.

key_points: MRI uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to create detailed images of internal organs and soft tissues
It is used to detect the exact location, size, and extent of tumours in internal organs without using radiation

sub_questions.solution: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to generate high-resolution images of internal organs and soft tissues. In cancer diagnosis, MRI is used to visualise the exact location, size, and extent of solid tumours in organs such as the brain, liver, and breast without using ionising radiation. It can also show whether the cancer has spread (metastasised) to surrounding tissues or lymph nodes.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is primary effluent passed into large aeration tanks ?

key_points: To stimulate the growth of useful aerobic microorganisms (aerobic bacteria and fungi) that form flocs
These microbes decompose organic matter in the sewage through aerobic respiration, reducing BOD (Biological Oxygen Demand)

sub_questions.solution: Primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks to facilitate the growth of aerobic microorganisms. Vigorous agitation and aeration of the effluent encourages aerobic bacteria and fungi to form flocs (mesh-like masses). These microbes consume and decompose the organic matter in the sewage through aerobic respiration, significantly reducing the Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) of the effluent and thereby treating it.

sub_questions.text: निर्मित 'अवसाद' को क्या कहते हैं ? इसके महत्त्व का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: What is the sediment formed, referred to as ? Mention its significance.

key_points: The sediment formed is called Activated sludge
Significance: A small portion is used as inoculum in aeration tanks; the rest is pumped into anaerobic sludge digesters where anaerobic bacteria digest it to produce biogas (methane)

sub_questions.solution: The sediment formed in the settling tanks is called Activated Sludge. Its significance is twofold: a small portion of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tanks as an inoculum to seed new effluent with active microorganisms. The major portion of the sludge is transferred to anaerobic sludge digesters where anaerobic bacteria decompose it to produce biogas (a mixture of methane, hydrogen sulphide, and CO2) that can be used as a source of energy.

sub_questions.text: उपचारित बहि:स्राव को प्राकृतिक जल स्रोतों में प्रवाहित करने से पूर्व निःसादन टैंक में अंतिम चरण की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the final step in the settling tank before the treated effluent is released into water bodies.

key_points: The treated effluent is passed through chlorination
Chlorine kills any remaining harmful pathogens/microorganisms before the effluent is released into natural water bodies

sub_questions.solution: The final step in the settling tank before releasing the treated effluent into natural water bodies is chlorination (disinfection). The treated effluent is passed through chlorine gas or chlorine-releasing compounds, which kill any remaining pathogens and harmful microorganisms. This ensures that the effluent released into rivers, lakes, or other natural water bodies does not cause water-borne disease outbreaks or environmental contamination.

sub_questions.text: विभिन्न जीव-जगतों के किन्हीं दो जीवों के नाम लिखिए जिनका आम तौर पर उपयोग जैव-उर्वरकों के रूप में किया जाता है। लिखिए कि इनमें से प्रत्येक जीव जैव-उर्वरक के रूप में कैसे कार्य करता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Name any two organisms commonly used as biofertilisers, belonging to different kingdoms. Write how each one acts as a biofertiliser.

key_points: 1. Rhizobium (Kingdom Bacteria / Monera) — forms root nodules in leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia, enriching soil nitrogen content
2. Mycorrhiza (Kingdom Fungi) — forms a symbiotic association with plant roots, increases surface area for water and mineral absorption, especially phosphorus, improving plant nutrition

sub_questions.solution: Two organisms from different kingdoms used as biofertilisers are: (1) Rhizobium (Kingdom Monera/Bacteria) — Rhizobium forms symbiotic associations (root nodules) with the roots of leguminous plants such as peas and beans. Within these nodules, it fixes atmospheric nitrogen (N2) into ammonia (NH3), which the plant uses for protein synthesis. This enriches the soil with nitrogenous compounds, reducing the need for chemical nitrogen fertilisers. (2) Mycorrhiza (Kingdom Fungi) — Mycorrhizal fungi form mutualistic associations with the roots of almost all higher plants. The fungal hyphae extend far into the soil, greatly increasing the effective surface area for water and mineral absorption. They are especially efficient at absorbing phosphorus and providing it to the plant. In return, the plant supplies organic carbon to the fungus. This enhances plant growth and reduces the need for phosphatic fertilisers.
